claim: The 13 mammalian phospholipase C (PLC) isozymes hydrolyze the minor membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to create the second messengers inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG).

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Gresset et al., 2012; Kadamur and Ross, 2013) and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: IP3 diffuses throughout the cytosol and binds to IP3-gated receptors in the endoplasmic reticulum, resulting in an increase in the concentration of intracellular calcium ions.

evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about IP3 signaling mechanisms.

claim: Phosphorylation and activation of the PLC-γ isozymes are mediated by two major classes of tyrosine kinases: receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) and soluble tyrosine kinases associated with immune receptors.

PLC-γ1 and PLC-γ2 are also phosphorylated by soluble tyrosine kinases associated with immune receptors, including members of the Src, Syk, and Tec families (Law et al., 1996; Nakanishi et al., 1993; Schaeffer et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Burgess et al., 1990; Vetter et al., 1991; Law et al., 1996; Nakanishi et al., 1993; Schaeffer et al., 1999).

source: Presumably, the intramolecular interaction between pTyr783 and the cSH2 domain drives a substantial conformational rearrangement resulting in activation of the enzyme.
